newsitem.title: JAPAN: SPEED SKATING-THIRD WIN FOR SCHENK.
newsitem.headline: SPEED SKATING-THIRD WIN FOR SCHENK.

text.p: German speed skater Franziska Schenk posted her third straight victory of the season on the first day of a two-day World Cup competition on Saturday.
Schenk, a Lillehammer Olympic bronze medallist, said a smoother style and lower crouch helped her to win easily over Japan's Shiho Kusunose in the women's 1,000 metres by 1.41 seconds.
Schenk crossed the line in one minute 20.45 seconds, a rink record at the outdoor Ikaho Highland Skate Centre north of Tokyo.
Defending World Cup champion Chris Witty of the United States was third on 1:22.38.
Schenk took both 1,000-metre races by more than a full second at last week's season's opener in Chonju, South Korea.
World record holder Hiroyasu Shimizu stumbled with a false start, yet managed to lead a Japanese one-two finish in the men's 500 metres with a time of 36.51 seconds.
Shimizu's effort was only 0.06 seconds better than compatriot Manabu Horii. Russian world sprint champion Sergey Klevchenya was third with a time of 36.63.
Norway's Grunde Njos, third in both 500 races at Chonju, failed to finish his race after crashing into the wall around the final bend. He did not compete in the 1,000.
In the women's 500, Japan's Kyoko Shimazaki gained her second win of the season with a rink record of 39.94 seconds, 0.13 seconds ahead of China's Xue Ruihong. Schenk was third in 40.09.
Kim Yoon-man gave South Korea their first World Cup win of the season with 1:14.39 in the men's 1,000, 0.07 seconds ahead of Klevchenya and 0.19 seconds faster than world record holder Horii.
